overview: Medical Affairs Approved Content Retrieval addresses staff search multiple approved sources manually and struggle to preserve permissions and version context in pharma and life sciences operations. The first proof of value uses approved medical statements, publications and inquiry logs. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is response time with verified citation coverage, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.
kpi: response time with verified citation coverage

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: approved medical statements, publications and inquiry logs; define response time with verified citation coverage and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Head of Quality / Clinical Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including golden question set with prompt-injection and authorization tests.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for response time with verified citation coverage
